name: Predictable password reset token
description:
The application's password reset tokens can be predicted: they are constant, derived from the server's clock, or a counter, possibly behind an encoding such as base64. An attacker who knows the model computes a victim's token without receiving the reset message and takes over the account.

burpsy reports this only after predicting the next token from earlier samples before requesting it, and the application then issuing a token within the predicted set.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no password-reset rows.
remediation: Generate reset tokens from a cryptographically secure random source with at least 128 bits of entropy, independent of user ids, time and counters. Store only a hash of the token, give it a short lifetime and make it single-use.

references.title: OWASP WSTG: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities (WSTG-ATHN-09)

vulnerabilityClassifications.title: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values
